labels.kicker: Do this in the Copilot app

appTasks.title: Install the app and sign in
steps: Download and install the GitHub Copilot app for your computer.
Open it and select **Sign in to GitHub**, then sign in with your GitHub account.
At **Connect your repositories**, leave every repository unselected and select **Continue**.
appTasks.why: Every chapter starts in the app: it’s where you give Copilot’s agents their orders.

seen.prompt: Which view does the app open once you’re in?
seen.explain: The app opens the **New** view. If it shows a short tip about a new feature, you can close it.

appTasks.title: Fork the course repository
steps: Open the course repository’s fork page on GitHub.com and create your fork.
Your fork is your own copy of the repository, under your GitHub account.
appTasks.why: Your practice work lands in your own copy, not the course’s.

appTasks.title: Add your fork under Sessions
steps: In the app, select **+** next to **Sessions**, then **Add GitHub repository**.
Type `copilot-app-for-beginners` and select your fork: the result that starts with your GitHub username.
appTasks.why: The app downloads a local copy (clones it), so its sessions can work in your repository.

seen.prompt: Where does your fork show up once it’s added?
seen.explain: The app clones your fork and adds the project to the sidebar, under **Sessions**.

appTasks.title: Start your setup session
steps: Point to `copilot-app-for-beginners` in the sidebar and select the **+** that appears next to it.
In the workspace selector below the prompt box, choose **Current checkout**.
Send the short prompt from your Logbook page: name the top-level folders, and don’t change any files.
appTasks.why: This one-time setup session uses the clone that’s already on your machine.

appTasks.title: Check your tools in Terminal
steps: Select **View** > **Toggle Review Panel**, then **Terminal** (no tab? **+**, then **Terminal**).
Run `git --version`, `node -v`, `npm -v` and `gh --version`. Each should print a version number.
Run `gh auth status` and check it shows the account that owns your fork.
appTasks.why: The setup script and later exercises use these tools, and GitHub CLI has its own sign-in.

seen.prompt: For `node -v`, what do you compare the first number with?

options.text: The **LTS** version on the Node.js download page

seen.explain: Compare the first number with the **LTS** version on the Node.js download page. If yours is lower, install the LTS version.

appTasks.title: Enable workflows on your fork
steps: In your browser, open your fork on GitHub.com and select the **Actions** tab.
If you see **Workflows aren't being run on this forked repository**, select **I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them**.
appTasks.why: New forks turn workflows off. With them on, GitHub runs the practice exercises’ automated checks.

appTasks.title: Run the setup script
steps: In the same **Terminal** tab, from the repository root, run `node .github/scripts/setup-training-scenarios.js --dry-run`.
Check that the `Repository:` line shows your fork.
Then run `node .github/scripts/setup-training-scenarios.js --yes` and wait for `Setup complete.`
appTasks.why: Later chapters use the labels, issues, practice branches and pull requests it makes in your fork.

seen.prompt: How does the dry run end?

options.text: `Dry run complete. No changes were made.`

seen.explain: The preview ends with `Dry run complete. No changes were made.` Only `--yes` creates the practice items, and ends with `Setup complete.`

appTasks.title: Ask the agent about the course
steps: Go back to the prompt box of your project session (not Terminal).
Send the overview prompt from your Logbook page: an overview of the course repository, focused on the learning path and `samples/book-app-web`.
appTasks.why: Requests for the agent go in the prompt box; commands go in Terminal.

seen.prompt: Which folder does the summary name as the web sample for later exercises?
seen.explain: The app should summarize the course structure and identify `samples/book-app-web` as the web sample used for later exercises.

appTasks.title: Ask a question in a chat
steps: Select **+** next to **Sessions**, then **Chat**.
Check that the project picker below the prompt box shows **Chat**.
Send the prompt on your Logbook page: when to use a chat, and when a project session.
appTasks.why: Chats are for questions: no branch, no worktree, and no files change.

seen.prompt: What does the app create for a chat?
seen.explain: The app doesn’t create a branch or worktree for a chat, and no files change.

appTasks.title: Tour the sample in your project session
steps: Go back to the project session you made in Chapter 00. It’s under `copilot-app-for-beginners` in the sidebar.
Send the tour prompt on your Logbook page.
appTasks.why: The tour gives you a picture of `samples/book-app-web` before the hands-on exercises.

seen.prompt: What should the tour refer to?
seen.explain: The app should describe the sample’s purpose, technologies, main files, data flow and tests, refer to paths under `samples/book-app-web`, and leave the files unchanged.

appTasks.title: Try the model controls
steps: In your project session, select **Interactive** mode below the prompt box.
Open the model control. Keep **Auto** or your current model, and the default effort.
Send the prompt on your Logbook page about how `filterBooks` searches.
appTasks.why: Keep the defaults for simple tasks, and you can change the model or effort mid-session.

seen.prompt: Which file should the answer refer to?
seen.explain: It should explain that search matches titles and authors without depending on letter case, and refer to `samples/book-app-web/src/App.tsx`.

appTasks.title: Switch back to New worktree
steps: Point to the `copilot-app-for-beginners` project and select **+**.
Open the workspace selector below the prompt box and choose **New worktree**. You don’t need to send a prompt: the app keeps the choice.
appTasks.why: The app remembers your last choice, and that was **Current checkout** in Chapter 00. A new worktree keeps each session’s changes out of your main checkout.

appTasks.title: Start a session from the practice branch
steps: Point to the project and select **Create from**. On **Branches**, select `practice-empty-state-copy`.
Set **Mode** to **Plan**, type `{issue}`, select **Improve the empty state copy**, and ask for a plan.
Exit plan mode, run the Book App and note the empty state, then ask it to implement the plan and compare.
appTasks.why: A session from a branch, with the issue attached as context, starts with everything the task needs.

seen.prompt: After the change, what does the empty-state message suggest?

options.text: Changing the search term, genre, or reading status

seen.explain: Reload and search again: the empty-state message should suggest changing the search term, genre, or reading status.

appTasks.title: Check the session with slash commands
steps: In the same session, send `/chronicle standup`.
Then send `/context`, and select the **Context** bar for its breakdown.
Ask Copilot to stop the session’s development server.
appTasks.why: They show what the session did, and how much context and AI credits it’s using.

options.text: The usage popup below the prompt box

seen.explain: `/context` opens the usage popup below the prompt box, with plan, session, token and context information.

appTasks.title: Your turn: a light and dark theme
steps: Select **Create from**, and on **Branches** select `main` for a new worktree session.
In **Plan** mode, attach `@samples/book-app-web/src` and ask for a small plan for a light and dark theme toggle, then implement it.
Check the diff and the preview in both themes, run the tests and build, then send `/chronicle standup`.
appTasks.why: The chapter’s whole workflow, on your own, without touching `main`.

objectives.text: Install and set up the GitHub Copilot app
Connect your fork of the course repository as a project and start a project session
Check the required tools in the app's **Terminal** tab
Run the setup script that creates the course's labels, practice issues, branches, and pull requests
Explain why you should use the GitHub Copilot app compared to using Copilot in an editor or Copilot CLI in the terminal
Identify key app features and settings
Choose between a chat and a project session for a task
Explain the session modes: Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot
Select a model and reasoning effort based on task complexity
Use prompt history to reuse and search previous prompts
Retry a response with a different model or reasoning effort
Start a worktree-backed session from a branch and attach an issue as context
Explain what a git worktree is and how it keeps each session's changes out of your `main` checkout
Add relevant context to a session so Copilot can understand the task and its supporting information
Use multiple ways to attach context: type `@` for files, `#` for issues, or drag and drop files from your computer
Decide between working in your current checkout, an isolated worktree, or a cloud sandbox
Use `/chronicle standup` and `/context` to review a session

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: The app as the control center for my agent work
The practice branches, issues and pull requests the setup script made

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: Keep my editor for deep coding, and open the app for agent work
Find my way by the work surfaces: New, Pull requests, Issues, Automations, Customize and Sessions
Chats for questions, project sessions for repository work
Interactive, Plan or Autopilot, for how much the agent does on its own
The default model and effort for simple tasks, more effort for complex work

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: Sessions as focused workspaces with their own branch, diff and history
A new worktree as my safe default
`@` for files, `#` for issues, `/` for commands

learned.Q0.2: You know how to install the app and sign in. Your sails are painted.
learned.Q0.3: You know how to fork the course and add your fork under Sessions.
learned.Q0.4: You know how to start a session on Current checkout and check your tools in Terminal.
learned.Q0.7: You know to turn workflows on first, then preview the setup script with --dry-run before --yes.
learned.Q0.8: You know a request for the agent goes in the prompt box, not Terminal.
